newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rebels shell army positions.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rebels shell army positions.

text.p: Separatist Tamil guerrillas shelled Sri Lankan army positions overnight as troops consolidated their gains in northern rebel areas, military officials said on Friday.

One soldier was killed and at least two were wounded as the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) directed artillery and mortar fire at the army-held towns of Omanthai and Rambaikulam in the rebels' northern Wanni heartland, they said.
"Explosions rocked the area throughout the night, but damage caused was not excessive," one official told Reuters.
The Defence Ministry said troops retaliated with artillery and mortar fire.

Troops sent out on patrol from captured areas killed two rebels, a ministry statement said. Soldiers who captured Omanthai and Rambaikulam, 17 km (10 miles) north of the government-controlled northern frontline town of Vavuniya, continued to fortify positions taken in a two-pronged thrust into the Wanni region.
"Clearing operations are going on in captured areas to flush out any terrorists hiding in those areas," the official said.

Two army divisions, consisting of some 20,000 troops, launched "Operation Jaya Sikuru", or "Sure of Victory", from Vavuniya 220 km (135 miles) north of Colombo, on May 13 in a bid to open a supply route to the Jaffna peninsula, 100 km (60 miles) further north.
The navy on Friday blamed the LTTE for an underwater explosion that damaged a ship carrying wheat to the eastern port of Trincomalee on Thursday.
"(LTTE) transmissions monitored by us indicate it was done by them," a navy spokesman told Reuters.
He said the explosion, which the navy believes was caused by a device fixed to the outside of the ship, damaged the vessel's engine room. "It could have been exploded by a timing device," he said.
The Greek-flagged ship with a cargo of 52,000 tonnes of Argentine wheat was anchored in the outer harbour at Trincomalee, 240 km (150 miles) northeast of Colombo, when the device exploded.
The ship was waiting to be towed into the harbour for unloading and repairs, the spokesman said.
The LTTE, fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in mainly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east, were not immediately available for comment.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war. The rebels say the toll is higher.
